data.narrative:
The Boring Company is a Series G-stage transportation infrastructure firm founded by Elon Musk, currently valued at $5.7B post-money and having raised $908M to date. The comparable universe in Transportation is limited, comprising two private peers (Rivian and Einride) with no public comps at similar stage or valuation tier, making traditional peer-median methods inapplicable.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method here. Using the last post-money valuation of $5.7B as the base and applying a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier for Series G advancement yields an implied valuation of $7.1B. This reflects the expected value accretion inherent in progression to a later funding stage absent material operational or market deterioration.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, produces a median estimate of $7.1B with a range of $6.1B (low) to $8.2B (high). This narrow methodological foundation represents the analysis's primary limitation. Validation would benefit from a broader peer set—particularly private or public transportation infrastructure or tunneling companies at comparable scale and maturity—or from operational metrics (revenue, capex deployment, project pipeline). The current range reflects stage-typical valuation growth but carries elevated uncertainty pending additional comparable data or forward-looking operating performance.
